context: A five-person old-school long-only manager, ~$400M AUM, 25-30 concentrated positions held three to five years. Two PMs, two analysts, one operations person. Tooling is Bloomberg, Excel, and filings; there are no engineers and no data scientists, and nobody here maintains a database. They buy research and datasets occasionally but cannot operate infrastructure. What kills them is being wrong about a business, not transaction costs. Anything proposed must be executable by one analyst and defensible to an investment committee that is skeptical of models it cannot inspect.
seed: Do monthly active users on a company's client-facing portal predict ARR for SaaS companies on seat-based pricing?
plan_A:
**Hypothesis.** For per-seat vendors, distinct monthly portal logins measure the billed unit: within a company, a 1% change in MAU implies a β% change in ARR one quarter or less later, β positive and residuals smaller than sell-side dispersion. MAU is not seats; the mechanism needs MAU-per-seat and price per seat drifting slowly. Null: MAU adds nothing beyond lagged ARR and company trend.

**Data.** 35–60 listed per-seat names: Atlassian, Asana, Monday, Smartsheet; Salesforce, HubSpot, ZoomInfo; Adobe, Figma; ServiceNow (CrowdStrike per-endpoint, likely excluded); Workday, Bill.com, Paycom, Paylocity; Zoom, RingCentral, Twilio Flex. Excluded: consumption meters (Snowflake, Datadog, MongoDB, Confluent), transaction meters (Shopify, Toast), admin-console portals. Rule fixed beforehand: seat-metered >70% of subscription revenue per 10-K or management, primarily in-browser. Authenticated hostnames only (app.\*, \*.my.\*, wildcard tenant subdomains), never marketing www; confirm wildcard rollup. MAU from distinct-user panels (Similarweb app-level uniques, Datos, Verto, Sensor Tower/data.ai where app usage is material), preferring exposed monthly panel size; two sources where available, disagreement flagging quality. Dependent variable, tier recorded: (1) disclosed ARR/ACV; (2) quarterly subscription revenue annualized; (3) total revenue less professional-services and license revenue; never mixed within a series (splice on an overlap ratio, or truncate). Actuals from 8-Ks, point-in-time stamped; consensus from Visible Alpha line items (subscription revenue, ARR, NRR, billings) at print morning, with contributor count and cross-analyst standard deviation; Bloomberg BEst fallback. Quarterly, MAU over each fiscal quarter's actual dates; ≥20 quarters targeted, under 12 dropped; ~2018 onward, 900–1,000 company-quarters.

**Estimation.** Log ARR on log MAU at h ∈ {0,1,2}, company and quarter indicators, within transformation. All three horizons plus a joint-lag specification, chosen on out-of-sample performance; expect β 0.4–0.8. Guards: CIPS panel unit-root and Westerlund cointegration tests, plus the error-correction form (Δlog ARR on Δlog MAU and the lagged level residual) if cointegrated; re-estimation in year-over-year log differences; company-specific linear trends, trading only the differenced or ECM result if β collapses. Cluster on company; also Driscoll–Kraay (Newey–West lags 2–3), wild cluster bootstrap (Rademacher, 999 reps) for β, Pesaran CD.

**Validation.** Random 20% company-quarter holdout, refit, level MAPE against the stated 3% bar; lead with three identically fit benchmarks: (A) ARR carried forward; (B) grown at trailing four-quarter average sequential growth; (C) two-way fixed effects without MAU. Claim survives only if the MAU model beats C out-of-sample under Diebold–Mariano on absolute-error differentials, clustered by quarter, p < 0.05; report the MAPE ratio. Random splits leak: keep as headline, gate on rolling-origin (train through T, predict T+1, last 12 quarters) and leave-one-company-out. In growth terms: median absolute year-over-year error below 150 bps and below cross-analyst consensus dispersion in ≥60% of company-quarters. Falsification: refit on the excluded consumption-priced names; equal performance sinks the thesis.

**Pitfalls.** Tracker re-basings give 10–30% step changes: screen with Bai–Perron on log levels, cross-check vendor notes, splice on an overlap ratio or drop pre-break history, never trade within two quarters of a break. Shelfware implies asymmetry: interact log MAU with a negative-year-over-year-MAU indicator; if the downside coefficient is smaller, restrict to positive surprises or split regimes. Price and mix drift raise ARR without logins: log price actions from Wayback pricing-page snapshots as a log price index control; else flag and exclude quarters after announced increases. Panel composition: enterprise SSO under-panelling versus SMB, deep-link misattribution, bots, moving desktop/mobile split; include app MAU or restrict to immaterial-mobile names, held fixed. Corporate actions and disclosure changes: event log, two-quarter exclusion either side. Process: ~40 effective clusters; horizon is fitted, so pick on rolling-origin and report all three; backfilled vendor histories need point-in-time snapshots or acknowledged lookahead; expect edge in smaller-cap names, decaying; split performance by year before scaling capital.
plan_B:
**Hypothesis.** Primary claim, gated first: for seat-based SaaS, YoY panel-MAU growth for the client-facing app is a contemporaneous, unbiased-up-to-scale proxy for YoY billable-seat growth. Secondary (conditional): ARR ≡ seats × revenue-per-seat, so the nowcast beats naive persistence proportionally to the seat share of ARR-growth variance. Kill criterion: gate failure yields a negative result plus a taxonomy of why, not a MAU-versus-revenue fallback.

**Data.** US/Israel-listed SaaS with per-seat list pricing and a distinguishable app host; exclude consumption-metered, transacted, end-customer portals. Gate sample = seat-like disclosers: ADP pays-per-control; Paycom/Paylocity clients × employees per client; Dayforce live customers and employees on platform; Dropbox paying users; Atlassian customers and seat-tier mix; Asana/monday.com customers above spend thresholds; Smartsheet ACV per domain customer; former S-1 disclosers; reseller price lists, Microsoft/Google marketplace tiers, G2/Gartner deployment fields (sanity checks only). Primary plus replication panel vendor (Similarweb, Comscore, M Science, Yipit-style) plus mobile (Sensor Tower, data.ai): monthly uniques, devices, sessions on authenticated post-login paths, stored as point-in-time vintages. As-reported fundamentals with dates: ARR or analogue (cRPO, subscription revenue, billings), seat/user/employee/customer counts, NRR, pricing changes, fiscal calendar, FX. Pre-print consensus snapshots. Scraped quarterly tier prices (Wayback).

**Methodology.** Calibrate: devices→users via vendor device graph or per-company deflator; winsorize MoM changes at 1/99 within company; inspect >25% breaks; coverage ratio (panel MAU/disclosed seats) trended per company: >~10%/yr drift kills level work, residual SD >~0.15 drops the company; fiscal quarter-average primary (pre-committed), final-month robustness. Gate, in YoY log differences, pooled with company fixed effects: g^seat=α_i+β·g^mau+γ_t+ε (γ_t common time effect, else a macro control: YoY US software/tech employment). OLS, Driscoll–Kraay SEs at Newey–West lag 4, 2,000-draw company-block bootstrap. Diagnostics: leads/lags one–two quarters (a lead becomes the nowcast core); negative-growth interaction; paid-surface split (admin console, SSO hosts), pipeline-wide if β and correlation rise. On a pass: Δ₄ln(ARR)=Δ₄ln(Seats)+Δ₄ln(ARR per seat), residual where disclosed, modeled where not; publish Var(g^ARR)=Var(g^seat)+Var(g^price)+2Cov per company and pooled, before model results; scope to seats where price/mix dominates; flag negative Cov. Nowcast Δ₄ln(ARR)_{i,t} five business days after quarter end, plus t+1: α_i+φ·Δ₄ln(ARR)_{t−1}+β₀·g^mau_t+β₁·g^mau_{t−1}+δ·Δ₄ln(price index)_t. Pooled fixed-effects ridge (penalty by nested CV on training folds only), then empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward pooled, weighted by within- over between-company variance. Keep the lagged dependent variable; add asymmetry where diagnosed; nothing else.

**Validation.** Gate needs all four: β̂ positive, nonzero at 5% under the block bootstrap, 90% interval excluding zero; β̂ in [0.5,1.5], β=1 tested separately; within-company partial correlation (time effects out) ≥0.45 pooled, positive for two-thirds of firms; halves within ~one bootstrap SE, sign holding; leave-one-out moving β̂ <30% and not flipping significance. Baselines: growth persistence; damped AR(1), pooled decay (the real baseline); pre-print consensus. Expanding walk-forward; no fold using vintages, restatements or hyperparameters postdating the forecast date; four-quarter tuning embargo. Report RMSE (growth points), MAE, RMSE ratios; Diebold–Mariano with Harvey–Leybourne–Newbold correction at NW lag 4 and Clark–West, block-bootstrapped by company. Success: ≥15% RMSE reduction versus damped persistence, Clark–West p<0.05, directional accuracy on growth-rate change >60%; else not demonstrated. Plus leave-one-company-out prediction; surprise-space regression of consensus surprise on model-minus-consensus (positive significant slope, >55% sign hits).

**Pitfalls.** Contracted seats versus active users (seats fall only at renewal; report downside β). Free tiers (paid-surface proxy, else exclude). Deskless and dormant seats. Enterprise blindness — managed devices, VPNs, SSO, desktop clients (coverage-trend warning, second vendor). Panel restatements and tagging breaks (vintages day one). Domain and product changes (event log, break tests). Disclosure endogeneity (keep every past discloser's full window; test β in a regime's last four quarters). Small N and specification search (pre-register thresholds, model, baseline; report specification count). ARR not standardized (redefinitions are breaks). FX and errors correlated through common tech headcount (constant currency or FX term).
